final_rationale: The verdict does not change because no genuinely new admissible evidence was provided. The Actor narrowed the claim and drew a sharper distinction between launch readiness and disclosure sufficiency, but that is a reinterpretation of the same record rather than new proof. That distinction is analytically useful, yet it is not enough for compliant_with_caveats here because the unresolved issue is not merely a narrative caveat; it is an unmet compliance predicate. The admissible evidence shows a material limitation affecting a named launch use case, an open legal question on disclosure, and a policy requiring disclosure unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. No evidence shows resolution, approved risk acceptance, or an actual disclosure record. Public governance guidance supports documentation and monitoring practices, but it cannot override the internal policy condition. On this record, certification framed as permissible without satisfying that predicate remains noncompliant.
remaining_concerns: The telehealth discharge planning segment is a named launch use case and is named in two clinic network commitments, which meets the materiality trigger.

The release policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch, and no such resolution, approved risk acceptance, or disclosure artifact is in evidence.
Legal review on whether the gap must be disclosed remains open, so the policy predicate is unresolved.
The 5% projected first-month traffic point may affect prioritization or proportionality, but it does not resolve materiality for a named launch use case under the stated policy.
Aggregate readiness passing threshold and no severity-one rehearsal incidents support overall readiness context, but they do not satisfy the specific internal disclosure predicate.
